scenes.heading: Clusters
scenes.subheading: The Spark compute behind your code
scenes.narration: A cluster is a set of virtual machines running Apache Spark that provides the compute power to execute your notebooks and jobs.

scenes.heading: Anatomy of a cluster
bullets: Worker nodes run tasks in parallel
scenes.narration: The driver node coordinates the job and hands out tasks. Worker nodes execute those tasks in parallel across your data. Autoscaling lets Databricks add or remove workers automatically to match the workload and control cost.

scenes.heading: All-purpose vs. job clusters
scenes.narration: All-purpose clusters are meant for interactive work and are often shared by a team during the day. Job clusters spin up for a single scheduled job and terminate when it finishes. Using job clusters for automation keeps costs lower because you only pay while the job runs.

scenes.text: Enable auto-termination so idle clusters shut down automatically and you stop paying for unused compute.
scenes.narration: Always enable auto-termination so idle clusters shut themselves down and you stop paying for compute you are not using.
